correctness_confidence.basis: A shared-pass/provenance-flag figure must occur only in the altered window. The zero correct-valued candidates across all 1,644 admissible pairs supports the checked-figure interpretation, conditional on the public preprocessing.

rigor.basis: The item-category recurrence correctly preserves both flag margins and error totals; the selective-corruption overlap bounds follow by filling exclusive cases first or last. The attainable extremes concern parser-compatible answers, including unusual comma padding.

novelty.basis: The original benchmark publishes discordant flag counts, while this analysis identifies when those counts are also wrong same-generation figures. Priority outside this particular benchmark and implementation has not been established.

significance.basis: The result changes how one may interpret the R1 gain and specifies what a replication should log. Its evidence is restricted to two panels and a single kind of numerical change with access to original passages.

reproducibility.basis: Source and dataset revisions are pinned. The replay distinguishes 413, 412 and 411 rows at successive eligibility stages. The three-page PDF is byte-reproducible, and no private model endpoint is required to check the counts.

summary: The three-page manuscript distinguishes a five-draw majority from the separate figure checked against a retrieved or original passage. It uses exact string geometry to identify the incremental catch count on the checked figure while preserving partial identification for the composite outcome. I inspected all three rendered pages, the frozen data-preparation replay and finite certificates, and participated in the same-context analysis and drafting.
strengths: Uses a sufficient condition valid over every admissible pair instead of inferring a joint outcome from marginal rates.
Provides attainable ranges for absolute checked errors as well as the identified incremental difference.
Explicitly explains why the R1 majority-based and checked-figure gains are different quantities.
weaknesses: Actual per-item generations were not recovered; outputs making the bounds sharp are hypothetical.
The broad extractor bounds include response formats unlikely to be common in practice.
The paper does not characterize other forms of modified evidence or verify the semantic correctness of a complete financial claim.
potential_errors: Applying the count of nine to wrong R1 majority figures would overstate what the available pairing identifies.
Using gold-passage string membership as proof of economic meaning would exceed the model of the check.
Treating reconstructed absolute intervals as unconditional on the historical panel ordering would remove a necessary qualification.
strong_novelty_candidates: Corpus-wide exclusion of a correct-valued altered-only figure in the pinned FinRank windows, leading to identified incremental wrong checked figures despite the separate generation.
